body:
closes #40631

## Problem

`'background'` auto-detection currently treats `SID_LUA=-8` as its own provenance (I use "provenance" here to refer to "originating source of data"). This works iff automatic OSC 11 writes & use Lua writes (i.e. `se bg=...`) can collapse to the same source.

This explains #40631; setting from `VIMINIT`, `--cmd`, `-c`, `nvim_exec_lua()` or `:luafile` can look like a value set by `defaults.lua` and is not picked up on by the bg detection, sotThe next OSC 11 response is then free to replace the user's choice.

## Solution

Make `SID_LUA` mean a **plain Lua chunk**, and add a `SID_DEFAULTS` for **internal writes that `defaults.lua` is allowed to replace**. A few examples best demonstrate this:

```
source                         last-set SID
automatic OSC 11 background    SID_DEFAULTS (-11)
Lua in VIMINIT                 SID_ENV (-4)
Lua in --cmd                   SID_CMDARG (-2)
Lua in -c                      SID_CARG (-3)
nvim_exec_lua()                SID_LUA (-8)
:luafile                       real script SID
```

`SID_LUA` is still the fallback for plain Lua chunks. Lua API calls now preserve the active startup/source context when one exists. Explicitly for example, this means `:luafile` uses a file-backed Lua script context instead of collapsing to `SID_LUA` as it did before.

comment_data.body: will a developer reading this in the future have any idea what this means :)

let's not keep adding stuff at the top-level `vim`, put somewhere in `vim._core` at least https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/556384200c2bc4be3154a32db51b19d9eb22a909/src/nvim/lua/executor.c#L904-L907

it's more like "internal", i think/hope? why would it be coupled to "defaults" specifically? if we want to convey a lifecycle, "init" might fit nicely?


```suggestion
#define SID_INIT    (-11)     // internal, during startup
```

@@ -292,6 +292,7 @@ EXTERN bool garbage_collect_at_exit INIT( = false);
 #define SID_LUA         (-8)      // for Lua scripts/chunks
 #define SID_API_CLIENT  (-9)      // for API clients
 #define SID_STR         (-10)     // for sourcing a string with no script item
+#define SID_DEFAULTS    (-11)     // for internal defaults

comment_data.body: feels a bit hacky, but if it allows us to put a nice fence around all such things then that is valuable. because it means we know exactly which things are contained in this hack, and can deal with it later if needed.
comment_data.diff_hunk:

             local luminance = (0.299 * rr) + (0.587 * gg) + (0.114 * bb)
             local bg = luminance < 0.5 and 'dark' or 'light'
             -- Use :noautocmd to suppress OptionSet event; OSC11 response may arrive after VimEnter.
-            vim.cmd('noautocmd set background=' .. bg)
+            -- Mark as defaults so later OSC 11 updates remain re-applicable.
+            vim._with_internal_sctx(function()

comment_data.body: made explicit i forgot i only defined this term in the pr desc... ty

`SID_DEFAULTS` means "this was set by automatic defaults logic, and later defaults logic may replace it" (Icleared up in the docs too just now). I couldn’t think of a better name, `SID_INIT` didn't seem right b/c OSC11 can run *after*
startup and stuff like `SID_{INTERNAL,AUTOMATIC}` felt too broad. 

LMK if you have a better name in mind.
